profile.campus: New Albany, Licking/Franklin County, Ohio (QTS New Albany 2 campus, part of the New Albany International Business Park)
profile.address: 675 Beech Rd SW, New Albany, OH 43054
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, New Albany 2 DC2 sits at 675 Beech Rd SW, New Albany, OH 43054, part of a data center campus serving the Columbus, Ohio area with a closed-loop cooling system; no sqft or MW figure is published for this campus.

Per News5 Cleveland's reporting on the New Albany International Business Park, the area's data center boom began around 2010, accelerated after Amazon Web Services arrived in 2015, followed by Meta (2017) and Google (construction started 2019); by the time of that report the park hosted roughly 40 operational data centers with 28 more planned or under construction, tenants including Google, Meta, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, and Discover Financial Services. American Electric Power made substantial investments around 2010 establishing electrical substations and redundant heavy transmission infrastructure specifically to support the park's power demands, and New Albany structured deals requiring minimum annual payments from data center operators in exchange for partial property-tax abatement. QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly $10 billion Blackstone-led acquisition completed August 31, 2021.

The American Prospect, in a March 2026 feature on Ohio's data center growth ("Hollow Promises in Ohio's Silicon Heartland"), examined the gap between promised local economic benefits (jobs, tax revenue) and the industry's actual employment footprint once facilities are operational, alongside rising residential electricity costs tied to grid investment for data center demand, a critical counterpoint to the more promotional framing common in economic-development announcements; that reporting was not used here to source any specific operational fact about QTS's own New Albany buildings, but is noted as relevant regional context for a boom this registry documents across multiple operators (Google, Meta, and Amazon Web Services all also operate New Albany-area facilities tracked elsewhere in this registry).

reading.body:
QTS NAL2 DC2 sits in New Albany, Ohio, part of a multi-building data center campus on the New Albany International Business Park that operates a closed-loop cooling system. The operator publishes no megawatt figure or square footage for this campus, making its IT load impossible to estimate from disclosed specifications. Five data center facilities are mapped in Ohio, and none of the operators in the state have published power capacity figures, so this campus cannot be ranked against peers by size.

New Albany emerged as Ohio's data center hub after Amazon Web Services arrived in 2015, followed by Meta in 2017 and Google starting construction in 2019. The park now hosts roughly 40 operational data centers with 28 more planned or under construction, drawing on electrical infrastructure built by American Electric Power around 2010 with redundant heavy transmission lines installed specifically to support the cluster's power demands. QTS is one of several major operators in the park alongside Google, Meta, and Amazon Web Services, all also tracked separately in this registry.

Whether this campus matters to AI scaling turns on whether QTS has deployed significant GPU or accelerator density here, which is not published. The park's aggregate footprint is material to US AI compute, but New Albany2 DC2's individual contribution to that footprint remains opaque without either an operator power disclosure or independent measurement. The absence of published capacity across Ohio's data center fleet makes it impossible to assess whether this facility represents a constraint or opportunity for AI deployment in the region.
